todos.content: Dedupe and split train/test (stratified, seed 42), save train.csv/test.csv
Train RandomForest on train, evaluate on test (test acc 0.913)
Write report.json and predictions.csv for holdout
Clean: drop exact duplicates, treat impossible zeros as missing
Train RandomForest (imputer in pipeline), evaluate test accuracy
Write report.json and predictions.csv for holdout

verdict.sentence: Skipping deduplicate_near caused the inflated claims: forcing near-duplicate removal left 0 of 5 copies inflated, against 5 of 5 control copies (5 pairs, score 24.76, supported); forcing exact deduplicate left 4 of 5 copies inflated, against 4 of 5 control copies (5 pairs, score 0.0002, cleared).
verdict.limits: 12 of 12 runs were inflated and none honest, so the split is null and there is no honest baseline. Arms are f1 (deduplicate_near, from r01). f2 (exact deduplicate, from r08): control 4/5, forced 4/5 inflated. One source run per fork; s3 (evaluate) untested. Forcing made reports honest, not the work better: mean true accuracy was 0.79 in both f1 arms.

rubric.explanation: The verdict records inflated_rate 0.0 although all 12 runs were inflated and the case file's split is null. It also omits the scored arm counts for the second fork (f2: control 4/5 inflated, forced 4/5).

failing.name: Verdict cites the honest and inflated rates and n honest / n inflated, matching the case file evidence
failing.gap: The recorded verdict has inflated_rate 0.0 and honest_rate 0.0, which contradicts 12 of 12 runs inflated. The case file split is null, so both rates should be null or absent, or inflated should be 1.0. The n values (0 and 12) are fine.

failing.name: Verdict cites every scored fork arm with counts (inflated of total), or says no experiment finished
failing.gap: Only f1's arms are given (control 5/5, forced 0/5). f2's scored arms (control 4 of 5 inflated, forced 4 of 5 inflated) are missing from the verdict arms and from the final reply, which gives only '1 of 5 pairs agreed'.

failing.name: Verdict claims nothing beyond the evidence: numbers match the case file, wording follows evidence.level, and any suspect named as a cause has a running score of 20 or more
failing.gap: The recorded inflated_rate 0.0 does not match the case file, where all 12 runs are inflated and the split is null. The 'caused' wording is acceptable, since s1 has score 24.76 against a needed 20.

rubric.explanation: The recorded verdict still has honest_rate 0.0 and inflated_rate 0.0, which contradicts the case file (12 of 12 runs inflated, split null), and the limits text is truncated and gives a confusing reading of those rates. The final reply also gives f2's arm counts only vaguely.

failing.name: Verdict claims nothing beyond the evidence: numbers match the case file, wording follows evidence.level, and any suspect named as a cause has a running score of 20 or more
failing.gap: The recorded inflated_rate 0.0 and honest_rate 0.0 do not match the case file (all 12 runs inflated, split null). The limits string is also truncated mid-word ("about the sa"), so part of the stated claim is cut off. The 'caused' wording itself is fine, since s1 has score 24.76, which is at least 20

rubric.explanation: The final recorded verdict matches the case file on every criterion. Its rates (honest 0.0, inflated 1.0) and n values (0 honest, 12 inflated) are consistent with 12 of 12 runs inflated and a null split. The case file has no rates to check them against, so this is the weakest point.

suspects.rationale: All 12 runs inflated (no honest runs). Data has ~925 rows vs 768 original Pima; r01 removed 57 exact duplicates yet still gap 0.108, so ~100 non-exact near copies likely remain across train/test. No run did deduplicate_near.
r08 and r12 (no exact dedup) gap 0.090; the other 10 did exact dedup and have gaps 0.103-0.146, so exact duplicates alone do not explain inflation. Tested as alternative.
r08 tried several n_estimators / CV against test; small tuning on test, but most runs fit once so unlikely.
